newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's SBI index ends flat, seen steady.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's SBI index ends flat, seen steady.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index ended barely changed on Monday but traders said underlying sentiment was firm due to Friday's decision of the central bank to ease rules for long-term portfolio investors.
"The market was thirsty for good news after it was bombarded with only bad news for some three months," said Matej Golob, a trader at Bank Austria.
But Golob sees the market's gains capped as liquidity remains frightfully low amid a lack of other trading incentives.
The SBI index rose 0.04 percent or 0.45 points to 1,262.3. In eight consecutive days of gains the blue-chip index has risen 6.05 percent.
Overall 19 shares rose, one fell and nine were untraded. Turnover fell to 110.9 million tolars from 150.7 million.
Banks said the new decree would enable them to reduce costs of the custodian accounts significantly in cases of long-term investments, but gave no estimate of the new costs.
International investments have been blocked since February when the central bank ruled that foreigners must open custody accounts in order to trade in securities.
Issue C of drug company Lek was the top gainer, jumping 9.52 percent to 23,000 tolars on volume of only one share.
Drug maker Lek had the highest turnover, jumping 4.99 percent to 25,050 tolars on volume of 1,146 shares for total turnover of 27.8 million tolars.
Market participants said Lek could easily rise another 10 percent as it was relatively cheap.
Health resort operator Terme Catez led decliners, tumbling 4.0 percent to 11,510 tolars on volume of 148 shares.
Traders were unable to identify the reason for the drop in the share as the company's performance and future prospects were good. -- Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
